title: AircraftClass
description: One aircraft type. Aircraft are INVENTORY, never part of a ship's designation (conventions 1.2), and enter no ship displacement figure. Embarked capacity is derived: hangar area / hangar_footprint_m2, rounded down (conventions 3).

designation.description: The navy's own designation, e.g. 'Type 38' (JPN) or 'F1' (USA bureau designation: mission letters + sequence).

role.description: universal_multirole is a doctrinal claim, not a convenience: every mission is a loadout state of one airframe.

powerplant.description: EITHER a `component` (an engine SKU, for a navy whose engines are swappable articles) OR a literal `spec` (for a navy where the airplane's engine is a property of the airplane and has no catalog line of its own). Exactly one; tools/validate.py enforces it.

component.description: Engine or turbojet SKU. One engine per aircraft type is doctrine in some navies; the data does not enforce it.

spec.description: Literal engine, for an aircraft whose powerplant is not a catalog SKU. Britain's aero engines are of this kind: the Fleet Air Arm buys airplanes, not engines, so no equipment line exists to point at.

refit_groups.description: Later powerplant generations available in the same mounting. The Powerplant row carries these inline exactly as a ship's Machinery row does — which is why engine codes never appear in possible_upgrades.

hangar_footprint_m2.description: Folded and packed. The divisor in the air-capacity rule.

max_alt_gear_kg.description: Max take-off weight in the alternate undercarriage state the Kits row names -- afloat for a wheeled type carrying a float kit, on wheels for a floatplane carrying a wheel exchange set. Present only on types that have such a kit.

derivation.description: How empty_kg was BUILT. ONE comparator -- the lightest real airplane of the class -- plus and minus the equipment that is SUBSTANTIALLY different, then a 5 percent modern-technique credit. ⚠ TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBER. (1) 'Substantially different' is NOT a neutral filter: the small items that get dropped are almost all things ours carries and the comparator does not -- beacon sets, catapult spools, extra tankage, span, high-lift devices -- so dropping them always makes ours LIGHTER, by 0.4 to 5.3 percent depending on the airplane. dropped_kg records how much, and it runs the same direction as the credit. (2) The credit is the HYDROFORMED PANEL LINE and nothing else: lighter engines are already counted as explicit line items, so they must not be used to justify the credit as well. Flush riveting and gap sealing are a DRAG credit, banked in the drag polar.

comparator.description: the lightest real airplane of the class

comparator_kg.description: its real published empty weight, never adjusted

added_kg.description: substantially different equipment ours carries and it does not — navalization included where it is land-based

not_carried_kg.description: substantially different equipment it carries and ours does not

dropped_kg.description: items judged not substantial and left out. ⚠ Record it: it is nearly all on the + side, so it is a systematic lightening, not rounding.

credit.description: modern technique — the hydroformed panel line — as a fraction of honest_kg

normal.description: Crew actually flown; may be fewer than seats.

speed_kmh.description: Keyed by condition, e.g. clean_at_6000m, with_torpedo, sea_level. A deception configuration gets its own keys.

combat_radius_km.description: Must equal ferry_km / 3 (conventions 4). tools/validate.py checks this.

armament.description: EXACTLY ONE of `component` (a SKU) or `spec` (a literal), the shape `powerplant` uses. A weapon under 20 mm earns no SKU, so it is stated here with its own mass and round mass and stays checkable.

stations.description: Ordnance stations. `alternatives` is the whole loadout question: one station, many mutually exclusive stores, chosen at spotting rather than in the design office.

form.description: The store form the station is cut for, e.g. 'torpedo' or '650_bomb'. Fit is by SHAPE, not by aircraft type — which is why a later airframe inherits the tanks for free.

rating_kg.description: Load limit PER RACK. A store must fit one rack, and the whole loadout must fit `racks` x this.

racks.description: How many separate racks the station is. Absent means a single point, where the per-rack and whole-station readings coincide.

alternatives.description: EXACTLY ONE of `component` or `spec` per alternative. A bomb under 300 kg earns no SKU and is stated as a literal with its mass, so the station-load check still reaches it.

kit.description: Air kit needed to carry it, where the catalog names one.

equipment.description: Fitted component SKUs (radar cells, beacon gear).

fittings.description: Fitted items too minor for a SKU -- a radio set, a plotting board. Stated with the installed mass the removed entry carried, so the specification survives the removal.

features.description: High-lift devices, speed brakes, canopy, ejection seat, pressurisation. CLmax follows the named high-lift device (conventions 8).

kits.description: Kit hardpoints and plumbing the airframe carries. Kits are FITTINGS, not upgrades: a kit code never appears in possible_upgrades.

deception.description: A configuration flown to be seen wrongly. Modeled because it changes measured performance and the observer's classification, and because struck-once is irreversible state.

struck_once.description: true = removing the rig is permanent and fleet-wide-visible.

possible_upgrades.description: Later generations of every family this sheet's own rows name, ordnance carried as stores included. Engine codes NEVER appear here (powerplant.refit_groups carries them); kit codes never appear here either.
